desc:
A vehicle drives from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell of a rectangular grid (0 = free, 1 = blocked), moving one cell right or one cell down per step and never entering a blocked cell. A turn happens when two consecutive moves go in different directions (right followed by down, or down followed by right). The first move is never a turn.

Return the number of routes that contain exactly k turns, modulo 1,000,000,007. If the start or the destination is blocked the answer is 0. In a 1×1 grid the only route makes no moves and has 0 turns.

grid = 3 rows x 4 columns, all free
k = 0 -> 0     (a straight line cannot reach the opposite corner)
k = 1 -> 2     (RRRDD and DDRRR)
k = 2 -> 3
k = 3 -> 4
k = 4 -> 1
hints: A plain cell count is not enough: to know whether the next move is a turn you must remember the direction of the previous move.
Keep two tables per cell, R[r][c][t] and D[r][c][t]: routes ending in (r, c) whose last move was right (or down) and that used t turns so far.

Entering (r, c) by a right move: R[r][c][t] = R[r][c-1][t] + D[r][c-1][t-1] (continuing straight keeps t, switching direction adds one). Down moves are symmetric. Seed the two first moves out of the start with t = 0.
editorial: Add the information the rule depends on to the state: the direction of the last move and the number of turns so far. For a free cell, routes whose last move was right come either from a cell on the left that was also entered by a right move (no new turn) or from one that was entered by a down move (a new turn). So R[r][c][t] = R[r][c-1][t] + D[r][c-1][t-1], and symmetrically D[r][c][t] = D[r-1][c][t] + R[r-1][c][t-1]. Blocked cells hold zeros.

The start cell has no previous move, so the first move is seeded directly: moving right into (0, 1) gives R = 1 at t = 0, and moving down into (1, 0) gives D = 1 at t = 0. The answer is R + D at the destination for t = k, plus the special case of a 1×1 grid. States: O(m · n · k); each is computed in O(1).
